title: Dynamic slot allocation & prefill-priority for continuous batching
creator: Avery Chen
description: Problem: We continue to see elevated tail latencies (p99) for mixed prefill/decode workloads in continuous batching. Root causes include head-of-line blocking from long-decode requests, suboptimal kernel selection for short-context attends, and naive admission that allows a few large requests to starve many small, latency-sensitive ones. Goal: Reduce p99 by 25% for our mixed workload benchmark while preserving throughput and unit cost. Approach: 1) Admission: introduce a dynamic slot allocator rather than fixed slots. Each GPU pool exposes logical slots with soft priorities; admission controller uses a multi-criteria score (tenant SLA weight, estimated token-length, current KV cache hit likelihood) to accept or defer requests. 2) Prefill vs decode priority queues: split queues into prefill-priority and decode-priority and add an aging mechanism so long-waiters cannot be starved. Prefill requests that are short (<=128 tokens) get a fast-path. 3) Kernel scoring: implement a lightweight per-request kernel-score computed from model profile metadata (attention type, sequence length, quantization profile) to choose kernels optimized for short vs long attention. 4) Attention heuristics: detect short-context patterns at prefill time and route to an attention-optimized kernel with SIMD-friendly layout; keep a fallback for long-context. 5) Prefill-decode pipelining: allow opportunistic decode-prefetching of KV chunks for anticipated next-token windows to hide scheduling jitter. 6) Backpressure & feedback: expose backpressure signals to the gateway so client-side retries and priority can be respected; record admission rejections and time-in-queue metrics. 7) Safety fallbacks: when p99 crosses threshold, automatically shift a percentage of traffic to a smaller, lower-latency model variant or enable decode-time early-exit heuristics. Metrics & Success Criteria: - p50/p95/p99 for prefill and decode phases separately - per-model throughput and cost/unit - fairness: 95% of tenants see <10% increase in median latency after allocation - no more than 3% throughput regression on heavy-batch benchmarks Rollout plan: feature-flag gated; staged canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback on p99 regressions; compare against baseline using perf-dashboard. Artifacts: design doc (Drive: /redwood/runtime/batching/dynamic-slot-allocation-v1), prototype PRs (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/4567), microbench scripts (/bench/continuous-batching/short-long-mix).
comments: 2025-02-12 - Triage: Problem reproducible on canary cluster. Initial spike analysis points to long-decode requests sitting at head-of-queue during continuous batching runs.
2025-02-18 - Design posted: dynamic-slot allocator with priority scoring for admission. Reviewed by Samir (RT) and Priya (SRE). Main feedback: ensure fairness across tenants; add hard max-wait guard.

2025-02-22 - Prototype implemented for admission scoring + split queues. Microbench harness run against short/long mixed workload. Result: p95 improved ~12% on a single-GPU pool; p99 improved ~18% for small models. Throughput unchanged within noise.

2025-02-25 - Kernel scoring hook added to runtime: uses model metadata (attention_type, seq_profiling) to pick 'short-attn' kernel when seq_len<=128. Microbench shows 8-10% latency improvement for prefill path on 'short' profiles.
2025-02-27 - Review comments from runtime team: need consistent benchmarking across quantized variants; request to add deterministic tie-breakers in score to prevent oscillation between kernels.

2025-03-01 - Integration test: aging mechanism added (max-wait=120ms) to prevent starvation; simulated heavy-load test passes without deadlocks. Added metrics: time_in_queue, admission_reason, kernel_chosen.

2025-03-03 - Planning canary: Gate behind feature flag 'dyn_slot_v1', will enable 5% of production traffic to start. Observability dashboard prepared (dash link: /dashboards/continuous-batching/dyn-slot-v1). Next: coordinate with infra for canary window and SRE rollback playbook.
Notes / Next steps: finalize PRs, add more model profiles to kernel database, run cross-region canary to validate routing/latency variance, write postmortem template for any canary regressions.
